findings.observation: Model keeps three distinct vehicle doors under a single pale fascia, narrow separator piers, a separate tall pedestrian recess and two broad south-wing window ribbons. The arrangement matches the 2018 frontal photo and the current 2025 oblique views.

Set-back upper glazing, open thin rail and thin projecting flat roof are visible in CPU front. Source bay doors are set back about the modeled 3 m and upper glazing about 4 m in the inspected builder. CPU cameras expose substantial roof area and hide most red soffit; request actual street-height front/oblique GPU views before final visual acceptance.

CPU front shows exposed blue-gray terrace, vehicle and south ribbon glass with red horizontal divisions. No obvious parent-wall burial is visible in these front images. Fractional first-hit checks are coordinator-supplied evidence, not independently rerun here.

CPU rear is predominantly plain stepped massing. Source record explicitly marks north/rear rhythm as inferred; no clear rear photo was provided. Do not claim exact rear fenestration matching. Inspect rotated gallery views for exposed side panes and retain stepped footprint.

Door and entrance bottoms align with shell base in isolated CPU images; references show level forecourt contact rather than raised stoep. CPU omits pavement, so actual game terrain contact remains pending.

Real red BRANDWEER lettering and fire-service badge are supported by both source dates. Model uses curved sans outlines on north fascia rather than invented building-name lettering. Arial Bold is explicitly approximate and subordinate district line is omitted. Glyph size is subordinate in CPU front, but actual GPU wall clearance still needs inspection.

Pale off-white/gray panel body, red door frames/soffit and dark glazing correspond to sources. CPU body reads warm gray under its simple lighting; no unsupported saturated wall color observed. Judge the red canopy visibility and realistic pale body under game lighting.
